paper.title: Learning to Bid in FCR Markets: A Best-of-Both-Worlds Approach

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated uniform-price auction (FCR) with stochastic opposing bids
unmapped: Bidding in a K-unit uniform-price auction (FCR reserve market reduced to uniform auction); actions are non-decreasing bid vectors on a price grid, mapped to binary vectors h in {0,1}^N with utility linear h^T W(beta)
Market-level feedback (clearing price and own allocation) from which semi-bandit outcomes on active coordinates are reconstructed
Utility per round lies in a range scaled by K (quasi-linear utility with known marginal costs in [0,1])
Learner knows its own marginal costs
settings.definition_quote: The opposing bids are stochastic. This setting is defined by $\mathcal{D}$, a distribution from which, for each timestep $t \in [T]$, the opposing bids $\betavec^t$ are sampled. ... Bandit Feedback: The principal only observes its allocation $x(\bvec^t,\betavec^t)$ and the price $p(\bvec^t,\betavec^t)$.

settings.name_in_paper: Repeated uniform-price auction (FCR) with adversarial opposing bids
unmapped: Bidding in a K-unit uniform-price auction (FCR reserve market reduced to uniform auction); actions are non-decreasing bid vectors on a price grid, mapped to binary vectors h in {0,1}^N with utility linear h^T W(beta)

settings.definition_quote: The opposing bids are adversarial. In this case, the opposing bids $(\betavec^t)_{t \in [T]}$ can be any fixed sequence.

algorithms.name: BOB Algorithm for Semi-Bandit (FTRL with hybrid Tsallis / log regulariser, Zimmert et al. 2019, adapted to bidding)

conditions: Assumptions 1-2: provider participates in one country; clearing price < 1

source.quote: The pseudo regret incurred by \autoref{algo : bob_bidder} is upper bounded, in the stochastic opposing bid case, by \tilde{R}_T = \mathcal{O} ( \log T ) and in the adversarial opposing bid case by R_T = \mathcal{O} ( \sqrt{T} ) where $\mathcal{O}$ hides problem-dependent constants.

results.notes: Stated as a simplified restatement of Theorem 2 of Zimmert et al. (2019) applied to the auction reformulation; O hides problem-dependent constants (gaps, N, K). Recorded as new because it is applied to the paper's setting. Compute polynomial per round is stated loosely (Frank-Wolfe with tractable LMO).

conditions: Assumptions 1-2: provider participates in one country; clearing price < 1

source.quote: The pseudo regret incurred by \autoref{algo : bob_bidder} is upper bounded, in the stochastic opposing bid case, by \tilde{R}_T = \mathcal{O} ( \log T ) and in the adversarial opposing bid case by R_T = \mathcal{O} ( \sqrt{T} ) where $\mathcal{O}$ hides problem-dependent constants.

results.notes: Regret R_T = sup_b E[sum u(b,beta^t) - sum u(b^t,beta^t)] against a fixed sequence, i.e. expected pseudo-regret vs best fixed bid. Constants (dependence on N, K) hidden.
